Dharmendra

धर्मेंद्र

The planet of raw physical strength sits in the one sign where it is strongest. India spent sixty-five years calling him the He-Man.

8 DEC 1935 – 24 NOV 2025 · BORN IN PUNJAB

TL;DR

Three planets at full power. Not one weak spot.

Most birth charts carry at least one planet stuck in its weakest sign. Dharmendra's janam kundli carries none. What it carries instead is Mars, exalted — the graha of physical strength, stamina and nerve — sitting in Capricorn, the single sign where Mars is at full power.
Two more are on home ground: Venus in Libra and Saturn in Aquarius, the planet of charm and the planet of endurance, each in a sign it owns outright.

So the scorecard on this birth chart is at least three planets at full strength and zero at their weakest — and the strongest of the three is the one that runs the body. He made his name shirtless in a 1966 film and was still working at 89.

The long arc

1935–1960 · PUNJAB TO BOMBAY

A farm boy, a magazine contest, a train

1958 Filmfare talent contest, second place
  • He was born on 8 December 1935 in Nasrali, a village in Ludhiana district, Punjab, and did much of his schooling in Phagwara — the town that still calls him its own.
  • In 1958 he entered a talent contest run by Filmfare magazine and placed second. It was enough to get him to Bombay, and it is the whole reason the career exists.
  • His first film, Dil Bhi Tera Hum Bhi Tere, released in 1960. It did not make him a star.
🔭 Nothing on this page dates these years astrologically, and nothing can. Without a birth minute the dasha clock has no calendar — everything astrological here comes from the signs, which the date settles by itself.
2
FILE PHOTO · APNE AUDIO LAUNCH · BOLLYWOOD HUNGAMA · CC BY 3.0
1960–1965 · THE WORKING YEARS

Six years of turning up

Bandini · Haqeeqat · Ayee Milan Ki Bela
  • Bimal Roy cast him in Bandini (1963). Chetan Anand put him in the war film Haqeeqat (1964). Neither made him a headline act.
  • Ayee Milan Ki Bela (1964) was the first film that got him properly noticed as a lead.
  • Five years in, he was a working actor in a crowded industry — not yet the name on the poster.
🔭 Saturn sits in Aquarius, a sign it owns. Traditionally that is the endurance placement — structure built slowly rather than a fast start. A resonance with a slow-burn first decade, never a cause of one.

1966–1974 · THE HE-MAN DECADE

Phool Aur Patthar, and everything after it

1966 the film that made him a star
  • O. P. Ralhan's Phool Aur Patthar (1966) was one of the biggest hits of its year. A bare-chested scene in it earned him the "He-Man" tag, and the tag outlived nearly everyone who coined it.
  • What followed was a decade of range rather than repetition: Satyakam (1969) for drama, Mera Gaon Mera Desh (1971) for action, Seeta Aur Geeta (1972) for romance, Chupke Chupke (1975) for pure comedy.
🔭 Mars exalted in Capricorn is the classical signature of physical power held under control — strength as discipline rather than temper. The nickname the whole country independently landed on is about as close to a receipt as a chart ever gets.

15 AUGUST 1975 · SHOLAY

Veeru

Sholay · 60 golden jubilees
  • Sholay released on 15 August 1975 and became the most-quoted Hindi film ever made. He played Veeru — the loud, funny, hopelessly romantic half of the pair.
  • It is worth noticing what the part actually is. In the biggest action film in Indian history, he is the comic romantic lead.
🔭 Venus in its own sign, Libra — charm and likeability at full strength, and the placement that fits Veeru far better than Mars does. Two planets on home ground, two very different registers.
5
PRESIDENT'S SECRETARIAT · GODL-INDIA · 4 APR 2012
1997–2026 · THE LONG LAST ACT

Parliament, character roles, and a last film

300+ films across sixty-five years
  • A Filmfare Lifetime Achievement Award came in 1997. In 2004 he was elected to the Lok Sabha from Bikaner, Rajasthan, and served that term until 2009.
  • Then a second career as a character actor — Life in a… Metro (2007), Yamla Pagla Deewana (2011), Rocky Aur Rani Kii Prem Kahaani (2023). India gave him the Padma Bhushan in 2012.
  • He died at his Mumbai home on 24 November 2025, aged 89. His last film, Ikkis — in which he played the father of Param Vir Chakra recipient Second Lieutenant Arun Khetarpal — released on 1 January 2026. The Padma Vibhushan was conferred on him posthumously that same month, received on his behalf by his family.
🔭 No astrological reading is offered for the end of his life, and none is implied. A chart computed without a birth time cannot date anything — and we would not frame a death that way even if it could.

A caution we would rather give you than bury: no birth time for Dharmendra was ever published. In the Rodden rating system astrologers use for source quality, that is a flat X — "no time known". It is also why you will not find a single dated dasha period on this page. Two boundaries sit inside his birth date itself: his Moon changes nakshatra at roughly 9:30 in the morning and changes sign at roughly 3:09 in the afternoon on 8 December 1935. Lessons 06 and 07 below explain exactly what each of those would change.

The honest bit

What a chart like this can speak to

This page does not do gossip, and on a memorial page it especially does not. Three things about his public record, and what the computed chart actually has to say about the pattern.

💪 Where the "He-Man" thing actually comes from
What's public

A bare-chested fight scene in Phool Aur Patthar (1966) gave Hindi cinema its first mass-market action-hero physique, and the nickname stuck for the next sixty years across more than 300 films.

What the chart shows

Mars is exalted in Capricorn — the graha of the body, strength and courage, in the one sign where it is at maximum. It is the only exalted planet in the chart, and there is no debilitated planet anywhere to drag against it.

⏳ A career that ran sixty-five years
What's public

He debuted in 1960 and was still shooting into his late eighties. His final film released in January 2026, after his death — a span almost nobody in any film industry manages.

What the chart shows

Saturn sits in Aquarius, a sign it owns. Saturn is the graha of time, patience and staying power, and on home ground it is read as durability rather than delay. Paired with an exalted Mars, the chart's two strongest placements are both about lasting.

🎭 The half of his work people quote least
What's public

Critics have long rated Bandini (1963), Satyakam (1969) and Chupke Chupke (1975) among his finest work — drama and comedy, not action. He was also widely known for his fondness for Urdu poetry.

What the chart shows

Venus in its own sign Libra is likeability at full strength. And Mercury and Jupiter are both combust in Scorpio — sitting so close to the Sun that classical texts treat them as absorbed into it. The traditional reading: the wit and the generosity register as part of the personality, not as separate credentials.

Being straight with you: everything in the left-hand boxes is public record. Everything in the right-hand boxes is a traditional reading of a chart computed from a birth date, offered for interest and education. It is not a claim about anyone's private life, it explains nothing that happened to him or to his family, and it is not a verdict on either.
Worth remembering

Two arcs that had no business working

🌾 → 🎬  A magazine contest was the entire plan

  • He came from a village in Ludhiana district with no film connections whatsoever, at a time when the industry ran almost entirely on who you already knew.
  • The route in was a talent contest run by a film magazine in 1958. He placed second, not first.
  • Second place was enough. It got him to Bombay, and the industry he arrived in kept him for the next sixty-five years.

🔭 The chart bit: Mars exalted, Venus and Saturn on home ground, nothing debilitated. A chart with no free gifts and no dead weight either — which is roughly what turning up to a magazine contest and staying sixty-five years looks like.

🎬 → 🎭  The second career, after the first one ended

  • The leading-man decades finished, as they finish for everyone, and through the late 1980s and 1990s his films drew steadily less attention.
  • Rather than stop, he changed jobs inside the same industry — supporting parts, comic parts, fathers and grandfathers, from Life in a… Metro (2007) onward.
  • The last of them, Ikkis, reached cinemas five weeks after he died.

🔭 The chart bit: Saturn in its own sign Aquarius. Saturn's whole department is the long game — the part of a life that is measured in decades rather than in seasons.

Actually learn this

Astrology, but make it make sense

Zero background needed. Read this once and you can decode the birth chart above yourself — no astrologer required.

LESSON 01

What a birth chart even is

A kundli, or janam kundli, is a photograph of the sky taken from the exact spot and second someone was born. Where each planet was sitting, frozen.

Vedic astrology treats that snapshot as the raw material a person was handed — not their fate, their starting kit.

His: 8 December 1935, in Punjab. That sky had Mars in Capricorn, Venus in Libra, Saturn in Aquarius, and the Sun with Mercury and Jupiter crowded together in Scorpio. Those placements do most of the talking on this page.
LESSON 02

The planets, and what each one does

Nine of them, or navagraha. Think of them as nine departments, each running one part of a life.

LESSON 03

Why "which sign" actually matters

Every planet has signs where it is comfortable and signs where it struggles. Same planet, different room, different output.

  • Exalted (best possible sign) — maximum strength. One sign per planet, and most charts don't have any planet in it.
  • Home ground (own sign) — the planet owns the place. Full strength, no permission needed.
  • Debilitated (weakest spot) — working with the handbrake on.
  • Everywhere else (neutral) — a guest. Functional, not special.
His scorecard is unusual in the opposite direction to most: one planet exalted (Mars), two on home ground (Venus, Saturn) — and zero debilitated. Three planets at full power and no weak link is not a common shape — and depending on an hour nobody recorded, his Moon may be exalted too. Lesson 07 explains that one.
LESSON 04

Combustion — when a planet gets swallowed by the Sun

This one is physical before it's astrological. When a planet sits very close to the Sun in the sky, you cannot see it — the glare eats it. Vedic astrology calls that state combust, or asta, and reads the planet as absorbed into the Sun's business rather than doing its own.

His: the Sun, Mercury and Jupiter are all bunched together in Scorpio, and both Mercury and Jupiter fall inside the combustion range. The classical reading is not "he wasn't clever or generous" — it's that those qualities show up fused into the personality rather than standing on their own.
LESSON 05

Dashas — why timing is normally the whole game

This is the part most people have never heard of, and normally it is the most useful thing in the system.

Planets don't all act at once. They take turns running a life, for years at a stretch, in a fixed order that the Moon's exact position at birth sets. Vedic astrology calls a planet's turn a dasha, and the full lifetime sequence is the Vimshottari dasha.

The order is a fixed wheel: Ketu → Venus → Sun → Moon → Mars → Rahu → Jupiter → Saturn → Mercury, then round again. Everybody runs the same wheel. All the Moon decides is where on it you start.
LESSON 06

Why this page has no dasha dates at all

Here is the bit that is specific to him, and it is the reason this page looks different from most celebrity kundli pages you'll find.

Which planet's dasha you start on is set by the nakshatra the Moon occupied at birth — one of 27 lunar mansions, each about 13°20' wide. The dates of every dasha after that are set by exactly how far through that nakshatra the Moon had travelled.

The Moon covers roughly 13 degrees a day. So across a single unknown birth date, the Moon can sweep nearly a whole nakshatra — which means the dasha dates slide by years, sometimes by more than a decade.

For him it is worse than usual. On 8 December 1935 the Moon crosses a nakshatra boundary at about 9:30am: born before it, his Moon is in Bharani (ruled by Venus) and his very first dasha is Venus's; born after it, the Moon is in Krittika (ruled by the Sun) and the first dasha is the Sun's.

What we can honestly publish: the order. After that first turn, both possibilities run the identical wheel — Sun → Moon → Mars → Rahu → Jupiter → Saturn → Mercury → Ketu → Venus. What we refuse to publish: a single date on it, or any claim that some event in his life fell in some particular period. Without a birth minute that would be invention dressed up as computation.
LESSON 07

The second boundary — his Moon sign itself

The nakshatra is not the only thing that moves on his birth date. His rashi — the Moon sign, which in Indian usage is what people usually mean by "his zodiac sign" — moves too.

On 8 December 1935 the Moon leaves Aries and enters Taurus at roughly 3:09pm. And it matters more than a coin flip: in Aries the Moon is a plain neutral placement, but in Taurus the Moon is exalted, at its strongest.

So a morning birth and an evening birth give genuinely different charts here. Nobody published which. We show both boxes on the chart above and decline to pick — because picking, and not saying so, is exactly what makes most celebrity astrology untrustworthy.
LESSON 08

So — was Dharmendra manglik?

It is one of the most-searched questions about almost every Indian public figure, and for him the honest answer is that it cannot be settled.

"Manglik" depends on which house Mars occupies — a specific short list of positions tied to marriage. Houses need the birth minute, because the rising sign changes roughly every two hours.

What we can say: his Mars sits in Capricorn, exalted — the strongest possible placement for Mars by sign. Whether that also lands in a manglik house depends entirely on an hour nobody has ever confirmed. Any site handing you a confident yes or no for him has quietly picked a birth time and isn't telling you which.

Quick answers

What people ask about his kundli

FAQ 01

What is Dharmendra's birth time?

There isn't one. No birth time for Dharmendra was ever published by any source, which astrologers record as a Rodden rating of X — "no time known". His date and place are solid: 8 December 1935, in Punjab. Everything on this page is computed from those two facts alone, which is why you will find his zodiac signs and nakshatra here but no lagna, no houses, no manglik verdict and no dated dasha periods.

FAQ 02

What is Dharmendra's zodiac sign and rashi?

Two different questions, and they have two different answers — which is where most of the confusion online comes from. His Sun sign in Vedic astrology is Scorpio, settled by the date alone. Western astrology, which uses the tropical zodiac rather than the sidereal one Indian astrology uses, puts the same birthday in Sagittarius; the two systems are about 24 degrees apart, so a difference of one sign is normal and neither is a mistake.

His rashi — the Moon sign, and what "zodiac sign" usually means in Indian usage — cannot be given as a single answer. His Moon crosses from Aries into Taurus at roughly 3:09pm on his birth date, and no birth time exists to say which side he was born on. Aries would make it a neutral Moon; Taurus would make it an exalted one.

FAQ 03

What is Dharmendra's nakshatra?

Either Bharani or Krittika, and the honest answer is that nobody can narrow it further. The Moon crosses from Bharani into Krittika at about 9:30 in the morning on 8 December 1935 — so a birth earlier that day gives Bharani, ruled by Venus, and a birth later that day gives Krittika, ruled by the Sun.

That single boundary is also what sets which planet's dasha his life started on, which is why this page publishes the dasha order and refuses to publish dasha dates. Lesson 06 above walks through exactly why.

FAQ 04

What does Dharmendra's kundli actually show without a birth time?

More than you might expect. Eight of the nine grahas hold their sign across the entire birth date, so the birth chart above is real computation, not a guess: Mars exalted in Capricorn, Venus in its own sign Libra, Saturn in its own sign Aquarius, the Sun with Mercury and Jupiter bunched in Scorpio with both of those combust, Rahu in Sagittarius and Ketu in Gemini. Not one planet in the chart is debilitated.

What a missing birth time costs you is the house layer — the lagna, the twelve houses, any manglik verdict, and every dasha date. That is a real loss and this page says so rather than filling the gap with an assumed time.

Method. Every placement on this page is computed with the Swiss Ephemeris using the Lahiri ayanamsa — the same engine behind every AxtroShastra report — from his birth date and Punjab birthplace. Because no birth time for him was ever published, we ran the chart at every quarter-hour across the whole of 8 December 1935 and publish only what held: eight of the nine grahas keep the same sign all day, so those are stated plainly, while the Moon's sign and nakshatra both change during the day and are shown as the two possibilities they are. We deliberately publish no house-based claim — no lagna, no houses, no manglik verdict — and no dated dasha periods, because dasha dates depend on the Moon's exact position within its nakshatra and therefore slide by years across an unknown birth time. The dasha lord order is real and is given; the calendar is not, and we do not invent one. His exact birth village is recorded variously as Nasrali in Ludhiana district with schooling in Phagwara; since this page makes no house-based claims, the difference between the two changes nothing computed here.

About this page. Dharmendra died on 24 November 2025 at the age of 89. This page is written as a memorial. Every fact about his life stated here is public record — his films, his awards, his term in the Lok Sabha, and his death. Nothing on this page comments on his private or family life, and no astrological reading anywhere on it is offered as an explanation, a cause or a prediction of anything that happened to him, least of all of his death. Astrological interpretation is for education and interest only. Our respects to his family.
